sections.title: Market Pulse: Post-Midterm Rally Ignites U.S. Equities

items.headline: U.S. Stocks Surge as Democrats Sweep Midterms and Oil Prices Tumble
items.summary: U.S. equities experienced a significant rally on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, as markets reacted positively to the Democratic Party securing control of both the House and the Senate in the midterm elections. This decisive outcome, coupled with a sharp decline in oil prices, fueled a broad-based surge across major indices. Investor sentiment was buoyed by President Trump's conciliatory comments post-election, signaling a potential for political stability. However, the AI sector saw some divergence, with concerns over potential regulatory scrutiny impacting data center and semiconductor-related stocks. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Cricut shares soared on strong revenue growth.
items.summary: Cricut ($CRCT) gained 48.99% by market close after the company reported an 11% increase in revenue.

items.headline: Duolingo shares surged on robust Q3 results.
items.summary: Duolingo ($DUOL) skyrocketed 19.38% in early trading following stronger-than-expected third-quarter results and raised full-year guidance.

items.headline: Uber climbs after reporting strong quarterly revenue.
items.summary: Uber Technologies ($UBER) rose 8.75% after announcing third-quarter revenue of $14.8 billion, a 10% year-over-year increase, and adjusted EBITDA growth of 31%.

items.headline: Nurix plunges as Sanofi ends drug program.
items.summary: Nurix ($NRIX) dropped 38.23% by market close after Sanofi ended a drug program related to the company.

items.headline: Hut 8 Mining Corporation falls amid AI data center concerns.
items.summary: Hut 8 Mining Corp. ($HUTG) fell 21.91% intraday as investors grew concerned about potential new limits on AI data centers following Democratic congressional victories.

items.headline: Nvidia declines as AI stocks face scrutiny.
items.summary: Nvidia ($NVDA) closed down 3.14% as part of a broader decline in AI-related infrastructure and semiconductor stocks facing potential regulatory scrutiny after the midterm elections.

items.headline: Democratic Midterm Sweep Fuels Market Optimism, but AI Sector Faces Scrutiny
items.summary: The Democratic Party's capture of both the U.S. House and Senate sparked a significant market rally, driven by expectations of potential policy gridlock and President Trump's conciliatory tone. However, the technology sector, particularly companies involved in AI data center development and semiconductors, faced headwinds due to concerns about increased regulatory oversight under the new Congress.

items.headline: Oil Prices Tumble Over 8% as Geopolitical Concerns Ease
items.summary: U.S. crude oil prices plummeted more than 8% today, with Brent crude falling to $94.51 per barrel. This sharp decline was attributed in part to Vice President JD Vance's comments linking his party's midterm losses to the ongoing Iran war, which helped ease geopolitical risk premiums.

items.headline: Consumer Discretionary Leads Gains, Energy Lags Significantly
items.summary: Consumer discretionary stocks were the top-performing sector, gaining 4.27% on the day. Conversely, the energy sector was the worst performer, dropping 4.73%, directly impacted by the sharp fall in oil prices. Solar power companies, dollar stores, and hospital owners also saw strong gains.

items.headline: Fed Holds Rates Steady, Treasury Issues Borrowing Estimates
items.summary: The Federal Reserve's previous FOMC statement on October 28, 2026, indicated interest rates were maintained at 3.75% to 4%, with economic activity expanding at a 'strong' pace despite elevated inflation. Today, the U.S. Treasury released additional financing details related to its Quarterly Refunding and provided estimates for privately-held net marketable borrowing for the upcoming quarters.

items.headline: Key Companies Report Strong Q3 Earnings, Boosting Individual Stocks
items.summary: Several major companies reported earnings today, with Duolingo ($DUOL), Kyndryl Holdings ($KD), and Procore Technologies ($PCOR) all surpassing analyst expectations. McDonald's ($MCD) beat earnings forecasts but missed on revenue, while Uber Technologies ($UBER) reported a 10% year-over-year increase in revenue.
